title: Spin-exchange interactions between circular Rydberg atoms over long times
authors: Andrés Durán-Hernández, Gautier Creutzer, Aurore Alice Young, Abderrahmane Kassid, Yohann Machu, Jean-Michel Raimond, Michel Brune, Clément Sayrin
abstract: Arrays of neutral atoms excited to Rydberg levels have emerged as one of the most promising platforms for quantum computation and simulation. With the hope to outperform classical devices, the number of atoms has been increased by orders of magnitude. However, the interaction time, i.e., the maximum accumulated time during which an atom interacts with its neighbours, has been limited to a few microseconds only. This restrains the number of gates per atom or prevents the simulation of long-time dynamics of quantum many-body systems. Here, we observe the spin-exchange interaction between two spin 1/2s encoded in laser-trapped circular Rydberg atoms over more than $60μs$ and 40 spin-oscillation periods, improving the state of the art by an order of magnitude. These unprecedented timescales allow us to record for weak atomic trapping a collapse and revival of the spin-exchange oscillation contrast induced by spin-motion coupling. Our results constitute the first observation of this coupling with laser-trapped Rydberg atoms. To counteract its detrimental effect for quantum simulation, we demonstrate a novel dynamical decoupling method that prevents the collapse of the spin oscillations. This method exploits the advantages of our recently developed hybrid platform that enables the measurement and the optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms with auxiliary Rydberg atoms. This work opens a direct route to long-duration quantum simulation of strongly-interacting many-body systems.
summary: This paper reports on observing spin-exchange interactions between circular Rydberg atoms for unprecedentedly long durations (over 60 $\mu$s). The researchers improved the coherence time by an order of magnitude and demonstrated a novel dynamical decoupling sequence. This work paves the way for long-duration quantum simulation of complex, strongly-interacting quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is extending the interaction time for quantum simulations using neutral atoms, as current Rydberg-based systems are limited to microsecond timescales.
main_result: The authors observed spin-exchange interactions over timescales exceeding 60 $\mu$s, improving the state-of-the-art by an order of magnitude, and demonstrated a novel dynamical decoupling technique to counteract spin-motion coupling.
method: The study uses laser-trapped circular Rydberg atoms to encode spin-1/2 qubits and measures the spin-exchange dynamics by monitoring the population imbalance over extended periods.
model_or_system: The platform utilizes laser-trapped circular Rydberg atoms, forming a hybrid system with auxiliary atoms. The interaction is governed by spin-exchange coupling, and the dynamics are analyzed by measuring the time evolution of the spin coherence.
key_observables: Spin-exchange oscillation contrast, population imbalance $M(\delta t)$, and the decay rate of the spin oscillations.
important_parameters: Interaction times exceeding 60 $\mu$s, 40 spin-oscillation periods, and the characteristic decay time $T_1 \approx 59 \mu s$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on post-selection via syndrome measurement to extend the effective qubit lifetime and models the decay due to spin-motion coupling.
figures_summary: Figures detail the physical setup, the quantum circuit sequence for state control and measurement, and the measured population imbalance $M(\delta t)$ showing exponential decay of oscillations over time.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, describes the quantum circuit sequence for state preparation and interaction, presents the measurement of the spin-exchange dynamics, and concludes with the demonstration of dynamical decoupling to preserve coherence.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the coherence time limitation in quantum simulation platforms, providing a concrete, experimentally validated method (dynamical decoupling) to extend interaction times for strongly-interacting many-body systems using Rydberg atoms.
